A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research and contain complete main text and Appendices A–E. Their text, equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic MoLRG experiments, image classification and segmentation evaluations, generalization studies, and appendix robustness experiments.

after.justification: v4 reports original synthetic and image-based experiments, including representation probing, generalization studies, ablations and label-noise comparisons.

M1.justification: The denoising objective and network parameterization in Equations (2), (4) and (5) are retained. Appendix B.4 also retains the same five-timestep ensemble with averaged prediction logits.

E1.justification: Both retain the same MoLRG scenarios and image datasets, including CIFAR, ImageNet and its evaluated subsets, CelebA/FFHQ, Oxford-IIIT Pet, Flowers102 and DTD. Training and evaluation task coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the DAE-versus-diffusion experiments, the MAE/EDM/DiT comparisons in Tables 1–2, and the logistic-versus-projection classifier comparison in Table 9.

E3.justification: Appendix D retains the same preprocessing, noise levels, model configurations, training budgets and evaluation procedures. For example, Figure 6 still uses 50M training images, and Figure 7's FID calculation still uses 50K generated samples.

E4.justification: Appendices B–C retain the clean-input tests, weight-sharing comparisons, DAE training ablations, assumption relaxations, separated-cluster experiment and projection-classifier analysis. None is newly introduced in v4.

E5.justification: Both disclose evaluation for Figure 3 on five MoLRG test datasets of 9,000 samples generated using five random seeds, reporting average accuracy and SNR. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain the same numerical entries and rankings. Figures 1–15 retain the same plots and qualitative examples; their embedded graphical content matches across versions.

T1.justification: The assumptions, SNR definition, propositions, theorems, lemmas and Appendix E derivations are mathematically unchanged. Differences in mathematical fonts and typesetting do not change their substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and Discussion retain the same claims about unimodality arising from denoising and class confidence, its association with generalization, and its disappearance during memorization.

C2.justification: Mechanistic interpretations and limitations are retained, including the simplified data/model assumptions, the need for broader theoretical foundations, and the disappearance of unimodality for well-separated clusters.

D1.justification: v4 adds the front-page statement 'Resources: To be released,' providing a limited availability disclosure absent from v3. Appendix D's implementation, hyperparameter, hardware and licensing information is unchanged; no actual resource release is established.

R1.justification: Both cite the same 104 works and retain the same research positioning in the Introduction and Appendix A. Changes to citation keys and bibliography formatting do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: v4 adds a contents page, keywords and correspondence metadata, revises author/affiliation presentation, and switches citation style. The body prose and sequence of scientific sections remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 applies a new visual template throughout, with a shaded title panel, lab logo, blue headings and references, revised typography and reflowed figures/tables. Figure 1 moves to the first page, and Tables 1–2 occupy separate pages instead of sharing one; their scientific content is retained.

improvement.justification: The new contents page and clearer visual hierarchy improve navigation through the main text and extensive appendices. Scientific arguments, experiments and results remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited to presentation and accessibility.
